notes: The colophon gives two eras: VS 1831 and ŚS 1697. In Caitrādi reckoning VS 1831 matches ŚS 1696, not 1697. In Kārttikādi reckoning (used in Gujarat), Āśvina of VS 1831 falls in Sept/Oct 1775 and matches ŚS 1697. So the two eras agree, and the date is about Oct 1775 CE. The weekday (Tuesday) was not checked. The text has a lacuna between 'rāvala' and 'śaṃbhūrāma', which may hide part of the name. 'Rāvala' is taken as a title or community name. 'gavaḍa' (in parentheses in the transcript; the catalogue reads 'Gabaḍa') is probably a surname or caste name; it might be Gauḍa, but that is uncertain. The names suggest a scribe from western India (Gujarat or Rajasthan) and not a Nepalese one.
